title: Nonnegativity of edge decoding value
statement: Let $G$ be a regular unique game with label set $ in q$. For any family of finite candidate-label sets, any default label, and any vertex and one of its neighbors, the expected agreement value obtained by independently choosing labels from the two candidate sets (using the default for an empty set) is nonnegative.
hypotheses_covered: A family of finite candidate-label sets indexed by vertices
A default label in $ in q$
A vertex and a neighbor of that vertex
